§9.3.4 SEC Period Tiers

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-sec-period-tiers · tables headers sec

✅ Normative

A financial period stack MUST be rendered as its printed tiers: period groups over their own date leaves, an apex qualifier above them, a stacked month and year joined into one leaf label, and the units note kept verbatim as the corner header cell.

This is the header stack of every 10-K and 10-Q. It looks ambiguous, but every part of it has a fixed answer.

| $ in millions |       Average for the        |  ← apex qualifier
|               | Three Months Ended | Year …  |  ← sibling period groups
|               | December | December | Dec…   |  ← stacked month/year =
|               | 2024     | 2023     | 2024   |    ONE leaf, joined
The page shows Requirement
"Three/Six Months Ended…", "Year(s) Ended…" MUST be sibling group tiers over their own date leaves
An apex qualifier like "Average for the" MUST be a tier above them, spanning the period groups
Stacked "December" / "2024" MUST be one leaf label, the lines joined
Bold on the current-period column styling, not structure: the header structure MUST NOT change; the bold is marked per cell as printed
"$ in millions" in the stub corner MUST be the corner header cell, kept verbatim

Why the stacked month and year join

"December" and "2024" are not two levels of anything — no other column shares a "December" parent. The typesetter broke one label across two lines to fit a narrow column, so it is a wrap. A tier is kept only for a label that genuinely spans more than one leaf column, as Multi-Row Header Tiers§9.3.3 requires.
